editorial.headline: Electronic Installation, With Bali’s Risk Gate in View
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 43213 covers electronic systems in buildings, airports and IT infrastructure, open nationally to foreign ownership of up to 100%.
editorial.body:
KBLI 43213 concerns the installation of electronic systems in both residential and non-residential buildings, as well as airport electronics and information technology infrastructure. Its practical scope is broad but specific: alarm systems, CCTV, sound systems, commercial management systems for prepaid electricity vouchers, access control, scoring boards, timing systems, perimeter pixel displays, master clocks and other electronic facilities all sit within it. The defining work is installation—putting those systems into place as part of a building, airport or technology environment.

The classification is open to businesses at every recorded scale: micro, small, medium and large. That matters because the activity is not framed as the preserve of only one size of enterprise. Its scope reaches from the electronics that shape access, security and communication within a property to the systems that coordinate information and display it in more complex settings. The record also identifies the applicable electronic-installation subclassification as IN006.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is direct. The activity is listed as open, with a maximum foreign ownership level of 100%. Put another way, this activity may be wholly foreign-owned under the national record. That position is sourced to Presidential Regulations 10/2021 and 49/2021, and it should be read as the national ownership setting—not as a shortcut around the separate local picture in Bali.

In Bali, the record’s status is **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**, rather than blocked. The provincial moratorium blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities across the island on a permanent basis. For this activity, however, the record states that OSS risk at the Large scale is Medium-High or High, and therefore it is not blocked by that moratorium. The honest conclusion is measured: nationally, foreign ownership may reach 100%; in Bali, this activity is recorded as not blocked by the moratorium because of its higher-risk position at the Large scale.
